messages.content:
## Responses as Code

Each turn, you take your turn by calling the `submit_program` tool. Its `program`
string is run as one PureScript program: pass one whole, legal
PureScript program — bare code, with no code fences around it and no
prose inside it — and it is processed exactly as written. All calls are
synchronous.

`submit_program` is the only tool in this session, and every reply must call it.
Each call is acknowledged with a tool result reading `ok`; what the program
produced arrives as separate messages after it. Text you write alongside the
call is recorded, but nothing reads code out of it: only the `program` string
runs. If one reply makes several `submit_program` calls, the programs run
sequentially, in order, every one of them.

Your program is compiled by `purs` before it runs. A program it refuses
is not executed: you get its diagnostics and submit another program.

## Views

Views are the only way to read data out of your code and are provided on the
turn after they're opened. Print statements are not shown.

Reading images is not supported.

## Language Rules

Your program is compiled verbatim, as one PureScript module: your own
`module … where` header, the `import` lines you need, and a `main :: Effect Unit`
written as a `do` block, which is where your work goes. The module name is yours
to pick. Import each module below under its own full name, as in
`import Gg.Files as Gg.Files`, so a module's path below is the expression you
write.

## Ending your session

Turns continue until you end your session.

A program that fails does not end your session: the ending it called is revoked.
Fix the fault and end your session in a program that runs to completion.

Call `Gg.Session.finish` with a short summary of what you did once the work is
complete.

## Your modules

Your program is given these modules:

- `Gg.Docs`: Find the callable surface, and take a documentation view back out of the window. — brought into scope with `import Gg.Docs as Gg.Docs`
- `Gg.Files`: Read, write, edit, search, list and walk the files of the workspace. — brought into scope with `import Gg.Files as Gg.Files`
- `Gg.Shell`: Run shell commands in the workspace. — brought into scope with `import Gg.Shell as Gg.Shell`
- `Gg.Views`: The only way material enters the context window. — brought into scope with `import Gg.Views as Gg.Views`
- `Gg.Session`: Ending the session, one group of calls per role. — brought into scope with `import Gg.Session as Gg.Session`

Search the documentation to find a function, by keyword or by naming modules
above. Open a documentation view of each function you intend to call, and write
the call on a later turn.

The SDK declares every function, whatever this run enabled, so a call to one this
run withheld compiles and then fails when it runs, naming the call. What you can
find in the documentation is what you can call.

## Messages you receive

Every message you receive is headed by one of the following labels, on its own
line — a view's label is followed by `: ` and the name it was opened under; a
file view's by `: `, its path, `:`, the 1-based inclusive line range shown and
the file's total line count — followed by a `----` rule and then the content:

- `Task` — the task you are working on, or a message from a parent agent
- `Compiler error` — your last program did not compile, so none of it ran; the message is the compiler's error and nothing else. Fix it and resend the whole program
- `Runtime error` — your last program compiled and then threw, or was stopped by a sandbox limit; the message is the error and nothing else. Whatever the program did before it threw stands, so do not repeat that work
- `Notice` — a process notice from the harness (a mode change, or guidance)
- `Summary` — a summary standing in for older turns the harness compacted out of the window
- `Documentation` — documentation or a skill you asked to read, delivered on the following turn
- `File` — a file, or a window of one, shown in your context — seeded by the run or opened by your own file-view call — headed by its path, the 1-based line range shown and the file's total line count, as `File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines` (a whole file's range runs `1-N`)
- `View` — a value your program put into your window; the view's label follows the heading, as `View: changed-files`

For example, lines 100 to 250 of a 400-line file you opened a view of arrive
as:

```
File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines
----
...those lines of the file...
```

A program that ran is not announced: the views it opened are the result.

Task
----
Create the file `notes/plan.md` in the workspace. Its required content is specified in `specs/plan-brief.md`, which is already open in your context. Write the file exactly as the brief specifies.

{"program":"module Main where

import Prelude

import Data.Foldable (for_)
import Effect (Effect)
import Gg.Docs as Gg.Docs
import Gg.Views as Gg.Views

modules :: Array String
modules =
  [ "Gg.Files"
  , "Gg.Shell"
  ]

functions :: Array String
functions =
  [ "Gg.Docs.search"
  , "Gg.Views.openDocsView"
  , "Gg.Views.openText"
  , "Gg.Views.openFile"
  , "Gg.Files.writeFile"
  ]

main :: Effect Unit
main = do
  void (Gg.Docs.search { modules, limit: 100 })
  for_ functions Gg.Views.openDocsView
"}

Documentation: Gg.Docs.search
----
search :: { query? :: String, modules? :: Array String, type? :: String, kind? :: Gg.Docs.DocKind, offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int } -> Effect Gg.Docs.DocSearch
  options: { query? :: String, modules? :: Array String, type? :: String, kind? :: Gg.Docs.DocKind, offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int } — The words, the filters and the page. Nothing in it is required and any of it may be left out, but a record that names neither a query nor a filter is refused.
    query?: String — The words to match, as a case-insensitive substring. It may be left out when a filter says what to look at instead.
    modules?: Array String — The modules to look inside, each named by gg's own id — `files`, `views`, `docs` — or by the path a program writes it as, `Gg.Files`, and matched exactly. Several are a union rather than an intersection, and with no query it is those modules' directories in full. A name no module has matches nothing rather than failing, and an empty array is no filter at all.
    type?: String — One type's name, narrowing to that type and to the functions that take or return it. Like `options.modules`, a name nothing declares matches nothing rather than failing.
    kind?: Gg.Docs.DocKind — Whether to return modules, functions or types. The default returns all three.
    offset?: Int — How many hits to skip, for reading past the first page. The default starts at the best hit.
    limit?: Int — The most hits to return. The default is gg's own page size and there is a ceiling above it, so comparing the hits against `total` is the only way to see a capped page. Zero is refused rather than read as "no cap".

Defined in `Gg.Docs`, brought into scope with `import Gg.Docs as Gg.Docs`.

Search every module this run bound, every function inside one, and every type they mention.

Matching is a case-insensitive substring over names, signatures, briefs and detailed descriptions, so `docs` finds `openDocsView`. Ranking is by the kind of evidence that matched: an entry whose own name matched outranks one that mentions the word in a paragraph, and a weaker kind never overtakes a stronger one however often it occurs.

Only entries this run bound are returned. The filters compose with each other and with the query, and every one of them, the query included, is optional.

The page comes back as a value and is also opened as a view under the selector `search results`. The next search replaces that view.

# Returns

The page that matched, best first. `total` counts every entry that matched before paging, so a page shorter than `total` is a page there is more of.

# Throws

`InvalidArgument` for a record that names neither a query nor a filter, and for a `limit` of zero. A module or type name gg does not hold matches nothing rather than failing.

----
data ApiErrorCode = InvalidArgument | NotFound | Conflict | Refused | Unavailable | LimitExceeded | IoError | OtherFailure

Defined in `Gg.Core`, brought into scope with `import Gg.Core as Gg.Core`.

Why a gg call failed.
  InvalidArgument — The arguments were malformed, ill-typed, or out of range.

It covers a path that is absolute or climbs out of the workspace, and an agent name this run does not declare.
  NotFound — The named thing does not exist.

A file, a skill, a memory, a task, an epic, an issue, a subagent, a stored program, or a documentation entry.
  Conflict — Well-formed, and in conflict with the current state.

An ambiguous edit, a dependency cycle, a duplicate id, a subagent that has already returned.
  Refused — gg refused the call on a rule about the session's state.

A compaction in flight that this call is not the one it asked for, a memory call while memories are read-only, a second ending or hand-over in a turn that already declared one, or a hook that blocked it. A ceiling that was reached is `LimitExceeded` rather than this.
  Unavailable — The call exists and this run's capability set does not offer it.

Every name in this SDK is in scope whatever a run enables, so a withheld call arrives as this rather than as a compile error.
  LimitExceeded — A gg-side ceiling was reached.

A shell timeout, a store cap, the delegation depth cap, or the run's wall-clock budget.
  IoError — The underlying input, output or process failed.
  OtherFailure — The failure was not classified.

Reserved for outcomes thrown outside a tool implementation. A capability that was withheld is `Unavailable` instead.

Documentation: Gg.Views.openFile
----
openFile :: String -> { offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int, maxLineChars? :: Int } -> Effect Gg.Files.FileRead
  path: String — The file to open, relative to the workspace or absolute.
  options: { offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int, maxLineChars? :: Int } — The window of lines to show, and how long a line of it may run; `{}` shows the whole file with its lines whole.
    offset?: Int — The 1-based line to start at.
    limit?: Int — How many lines to show from `offset`.
    maxLineChars?: Int — The most characters a line of the view may run to, from 1 to 65536; a longer line is cut there and annotated in place as `(N more chars...)`. Left out, lines arrive whole, and neither the returned contents nor the file is cut.

Defined in `Gg.Views`, brought into scope with `import Gg.Views as Gg.Views`.

Read a file and place it in the context window, keyed by its path.

The file becomes its own context item, attributed to its path and filed under it. `offset` and `limit` select a window of lines, and two pages of one file are two views that coexist; re-opening the same page replaces what it showed. An image file is displayed as a picture, and this is the only call that displays one.

A text view's body is held to a 65,536-byte cap: a window that would carry more is refused with its size and the bound, and nothing is opened and nothing is truncated. `maxLineChars` cuts each line of the view longer than that many characters at that point and annotates it in place as `foo (123 more chars...)`; left out, lines arrive whole. The cut is the view's alone — the value this call hands back and the file itself are untouched — and the cap is measured against the body after it.

# Returns

The `TextFile` arm for a text file's window, or the `ImageFile` arm describing a picture whose bytes never entered the program.

# Throws

`LimitExceeded`, naming the size and the bound, for a text view whose body — after any cut — would exceed 65,536 bytes; nothing is opened. `InvalidArgument` for a `maxLineChars` of zero or above 65,536, and `NotFound` for a missing path.

# Inventory brief

Write `notes/inventory.md` describing the workspace root.

## Required content

1. A top-level heading reading `# Workspace inventory`.
2. One Markdown list entry per entry of the workspace's top-level
   directory, in the order the listing returns them.
3. Each entry formatted as `- `, the entry's name, then ` (dir)` for a
   directory or ` (file)` for a file.

## Rules

- List the top-level directory only; do not recurse.
- Create the `notes/` directory as part of the write if it does not exist.
- Change nothing else in the workspace.

Each turn, you take your turn by calling the `submit_program` tool. Its `program`
string is run as one PureScript program: pass one whole, legal
PureScript program — bare code, with no code fences around it and no
prose inside it — and it is processed exactly as written. All calls are
synchronous.

`submit_program` is the only tool in this session, and every reply must call it.
Each call is acknowledged with a tool result reading `ok`; what the program
produced arrives as separate messages after it. Text you write alongside the
call is recorded, but nothing reads code out of it: only the `program` string
runs. If one reply makes several `submit_program` calls, the programs run
sequentially, in order, every one of them.

Your program is compiled by `purs` before it runs. A program it refuses
is not executed: you get its diagnostics and submit another program.

## Views

Views are the only way to read data out of your code and are provided on the
turn after they're opened. Print statements are not shown.

Reading images is not supported.

## Language Rules

Your program is compiled verbatim, as one PureScript module: your own
`module … where` header, the `import` lines you need, and a `main :: Effect Unit`
written as a `do` block, which is where your work goes. The module name is yours
to pick. Import each module below under its own full name, as in

write.

Documentation: Gg.Docs.search
----
search :: { query? :: String, modules? :: Array String, type? :: String, kind? :: Gg.Docs.DocKind, offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int } -> Effect Gg.Docs.DocSearch
  options: { query? :: String, modules? :: Array String, type? :: String, kind? :: Gg.Docs.DocKind, offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int } — The words, the filters and the page. Nothing in it is required and any of it may be left out, but a record that names neither a query nor a filter is refused.
    query?: String — The words to match, as a case-insensitive substring. It may be left out when a filter says what to look at instead.
    modules?: Array String — The modules to look inside, each named by gg's own id — `files`, `views`, `docs` — or by the path a program writes it as, `Gg.Files`, and matched exactly. Several are a union rather than an intersection, and with no query it is those modules' directories in full. A name no module has matches nothing rather than failing, and an empty array is no filter at all.
    type?: String — One type's name, narrowing to that type and to the functions that take or return it. Like `options.modules`, a name nothing declares matches nothing rather than failing.
    kind?: Gg.Docs.DocKind — Whether to return modules, functions or types. The default returns all three.
    offset?: Int — How many hits to skip, for reading past the first page. The default starts at the best hit.
    limit?: Int — The most hits to return. The default is gg's own page size and there is a ceiling above it, so comparing the hits against `total` is the only way to see a capped page. Zero is refused rather than read as "no cap".

Defined in `Gg.Docs`, brought into scope with `import Gg.Docs as Gg.Docs`.

Search every module this run bound, every function inside one, and every type they mention.

Matching is a case-insensitive substring over names, signatures, briefs and detailed descriptions, so `docs` finds `openDocsView`. Ranking is by the kind of evidence that matched: an entry whose own name matched outranks one that mentions the word in a paragraph, and a weaker kind never overtakes a stronger one however often it occurs.

Only entries this run bound are returned. The filters compose with each other and with the query, and every one of them, the query included, is optional.

The page comes back as a value and is also opened as a view under the selector `search results`. The next search replaces that view.

# Returns

The page that matched, best first. `total` counts every entry that matched before paging, so a page shorter than `total` is a page there is more of.

# Throws

`InvalidArgument` for a record that names neither a query nor a filter, and for a `limit` of zero. A module or type name gg does not hold matches nothing rather than failing.

Documentation: Gg.Core.ApiErrorCode
----
data ApiErrorCode = InvalidArgument | NotFound | Conflict | Refused | Unavailable | LimitExceeded | IoError | OtherFailure

Defined in `Gg.Core`, brought into scope with `import Gg.Core as Gg.Core`.

Why a gg call failed.
  InvalidArgument — The arguments were malformed, ill-typed, or out of range.

It covers a path that is absolute or climbs out of the workspace, and an agent name this run does not declare.
  NotFound — The named thing does not exist.

A file, a skill, a memory, a task, an epic, an issue, a subagent, a stored program, or a documentation entry.
  Conflict — Well-formed, and in conflict with the current state.

An ambiguous edit, a dependency cycle, a duplicate id, a subagent that has already returned.
  Refused — gg refused the call on a rule about the session's state.

A compaction in flight that this call is not the one it asked for, a memory call while memories are read-only, a second ending or hand-over in a turn that already declared one, or a hook that blocked it. A ceiling that was reached is `LimitExceeded` rather than this.
  Unavailable — The call exists and this run's capability set does not offer it.

Every name in this SDK is in scope whatever a run enables, so a withheld call arrives as this rather than as a compile error.
  LimitExceeded — A gg-side ceiling was reached.

A shell timeout, a store cap, the delegation depth cap, or the run's wall-clock budget.
  IoError — The underlying input, output or process failed.
  OtherFailure — The failure was not classified.

Reserved for outcomes thrown outside a tool implementation. A capability that was withheld is `Unavailable` instead.

Documentation: Gg.Views.openFile
----
openFile :: String -> { offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int, maxLineChars? :: Int } -> Effect Gg.Files.FileRead
  path: String — The file to open, relative to the workspace or absolute.
  options: { offset? :: Int, limit? :: Int, maxLineChars? :: Int } — The window of lines to show, and how long a line of it may run; `{}` shows the whole file with its lines whole.
    offset?: Int — The 1-based line to start at.
    limit?: Int — How many lines to show from `offset`.
    maxLineChars?: Int — The most characters a line of the view may run to, from 1 to 65536; a longer line is cut there and annotated in place as `(N more chars...)`. Left out, lines arrive whole, and neither the returned contents nor the file is cut.

Defined in `Gg.Views`, brought into scope with `import Gg.Views as Gg.Views`.

Read a file and place it in the context window, keyed by its path.

The file becomes its own context item, attributed to its path and filed under it. `offset` and `limit` select a window of lines, and two pages of one file are two views that coexist; re-opening the same page replaces what it showed. An image file is displayed as a picture, and this is the only call that displays one.

A text view's body is held to a 65,536-byte cap: a window that would carry more is refused with its size and the bound, and nothing is opened and nothing is truncated. `maxLineChars` cuts each line of the view longer than that many characters at that point and annotates it in place as `foo (123 more chars...)`; left out, lines arrive whole. The cut is the view's alone — the value this call hands back and the file itself are untouched — and the cap is measured against the body after it.

# Returns

The `TextFile` arm for a text file's window, or the `ImageFile` arm describing a picture whose bytes never entered the program.

# Throws

`LimitExceeded`, naming the size and the bound, for a text view whose body — after any cut — would exceed 65,536 bytes; nothing is opened. `InvalidArgument` for a `maxLineChars` of zero or above 65,536, and `NotFound` for a missing path.
